What we know about “Nur Omar Mohamed’s military career” in the Somali army makes it “very doubtful” that Rep. Ilhan Omar’s father “met the US legal definition of a ‘refugee’,” argues National Review’s Jim Geraghty. One obituary noted that his “prestigious career in the military ended in 1991 after the Barre regime was ousted.” Notes Geraghty: “The Somali government was using its military to commit genocide for the better part of three decades, intensifying in the late 1980s.” Credible sources discredit the notion that her father could “rise to the rank of colonel with no role in that military’s massive-scale genocide.” How was a Somali colonel “qualified as a refugee” when he may have “ordered, incited, assisted or otherwise participated in the persecution” of civilians?

President Trump “has been widely mocked for asking voters to ‘pretend I’m on the ballot,’ ” notes the Washington Examiner’s Byron York. Yet appealing to “low-propensity voters” — such one ones who won’t normally vote unless Trump’s on the ballot — “makes sense.” A 2025 Pew Research study found eligible voters nationwide who didn’t vote in 2020 and ’22 but did in ’24 backed Trump 55%-41%. “This was not just a tiny group of people”: “2024-only voters made up 12% of the entire electorate in the presidential race that year. It made a big difference for Trump.” So, “if Republicans are trying to turn out low-propensity voters” now, “it makes sense to ask them to pretend that Trump is on the ballot.”

“Democrats should think hard about” the “broad spectrum of sketchy fundraising behavior, from outright scams to bad ideas,” argues Slow Boring’s Matt Yglesias after getting a “rather absurd request” from Gov. Maura Healy (D-Mass.), who’s in zero danger of losing. People “acutely frightened about the state of our country” must “be smart with our resources, not throwing them at dumb stuff” like unwinnable or unlosable races, or ones without “large strategic implications.” Never forget: “People make money off of political campaigns” — “vendors and consultants” who “benefit specifically from donations” to candidates who’ve hired them, “even if other candidates would be a better use of your money.” And “outright scams” include “PACs that say they’re supporting candidates but mostly just fund themselves.” To keep “the small-donor engine running,” Democrats should be “giving donors some assurances that their money is being well spent.”

The major political parties “keep force-feeding us s—t sandwiches and telling us to like them,” fumes Erick Erickson at The Free Press, and insisting that “we must debase ourselves a little further every cycle.” We’re told to “hold our noses” and “pull the lever” for “white nationalists, racists, and antisemites” and “crooks, frauds, charlatans, and those who’d attack the victim of molestation,” or else face “the end of America.” We “have heard that message every two years for 20 years,” but “America is still here” even as the “candidates keep getting worse.” No! Of every election requires us to swallow something rotten, we might as well starve.” America will never be made “great again” if we are “continually descending into the sewer to find candidates.”

María Corina Machado’s return to Venezuela “poses a challenge to the ruling regime of Delcy Rodríguez, but also to the Trump Administration,” frets The Wall Street Journal’s Editorial Board. Machado had left “the country in fear for her life” but now as promised has returned “to participate in a transition back to democracy” following former President Nicolás Maduro’s arrest. But Rodríguez “refuses to set a date for new elections.” Amid that stall, Secretary of State Marco Rubio and President Trump must ensure Machado’s safety: “It’s all too easy to imagine her suddenly dying in a car ‘accident’ or from a mysterious illness” — and Trump’s Venezuelan oil deal “won’t be worth much unless Venezuela has a government with democratic legitimacy,” something “that should start with a date and a credible process for a free and fair democratic election.”

— Compiled by The Post Editorial Board
news.content: از پوشش ما در نتایج جستجوی خود بیشتر مشاهده کنید. جیم گراتی از نشنال ریویو استدلال می کند که آنچه که ما در مورد "کارنامه نظامی نور عمر محمد" در ارتش سومالی می دانیم، "بسیار مشکوک" می کند که پدر نماینده ایلهان عمر "با تعریف قانونی ایالات متحده از "پناهنده" مطابقت داشته باشد. یکی از آگهی‌های ترحیم اشاره کرد که «کار معتبر او در ارتش در سال 1991 پس از سرنگونی رژیم باره به پایان رسید. گرااتی خاطرنشان می کند: «دولت سومالی از ارتش خود برای ارتکاب نسل کشی برای سه دهه استفاده می کرد که در اواخر دهه 1980 تشدید شد.» منابع موثق این تصور را که پدرش می‌تواند «بدون هیچ نقشی در نسل‌کشی گسترده ارتش به درجه سرهنگی برسد، بی‌اعتبار می‌کند. یک سرهنگ سومالیایی چگونه "واجد شرایط پناهندگی" بود، در حالی که ممکن است "دستور، تحریک، کمک یا مشارکت در آزار و شکنجه" غیرنظامیان را داده باشد؟ رئیس جمهور ترامپ "به طور گسترده به دلیل درخواست از رای دهندگان برای "تظاهر به من در برگه رای" مورد تمسخر قرار گرفته است. به طور معمول رای نمی دهد مگر اینکه ترامپ در برگه رای باشد - «معنی است. یک مطالعه تحقیقاتی Pew در سال 2025 نشان داد که رای دهندگان واجد شرایط در سراسر کشور که در سال های 2020 و 22 رای ندادند، اما در سال 24 رای دادند، 55٪ تا 41٪ از ترامپ حمایت کردند. "این فقط یک گروه کوچک از مردم نبودند": "رای دهندگان تنها در 2024 12٪ از کل رای دهندگان را در رقابت های ریاست جمهوری آن سال تشکیل می دادند. این یک تفاوت بزرگ برای ترامپ ایجاد کرد.» بنابراین، "اگر جمهوری خواهان اکنون در تلاش هستند تا رای دهندگان کم گرایش را به خود جلب کنند"، "منطقی است که از آنها بخواهیم به روابط عمومی بپردازند."

Russian forces launched strikes on Monday on Kharkiv, Ukraine’s second-largest city, killing two people and injuring four, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said on Telegram.

Terekhov said there had been three strikes on a city district and that a high-rise apartment block and private homes had been damaged.

Regional Governor Oleh Syniehubov said Russian forces had launched missiles at the city, a frequent target of attacks about 30 km (18 miles) from the Russian border.

In neighboring Dnipropetrovsk region, Governor Oleksandr Hanzha said Russian forces had launched more than 50 drone and artillery attacks.

A drone strike in the city of Pavlohrad killed one person and wounded 10, he said. Three of the injured were seriously hurt.
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. نیروهای روسی روز دوشنبه حملاتی را به خارکف، دومین شهر بزرگ اوکراین انجام دادند که منجر به کشته شدن دو نفر و زخمی شدن چهار نفر شد. فرماندار منطقه اوله سینیهوبوف گفت که نیروهای روسی موشک هایی را به سمت شهر شلیک کرده اند که هدف مکرر حملات در حدود 30 کیلومتری مرز روسیه است. در منطقه همسایه دنیپروپتروفسک، الکساندر هانژا فرماندار گفت که نیروهای روسی بیش از 50 حمله پهپادی و توپخانه ای شلیک کرده اند. حمله یک هواپیمای بدون سرنشین در شهر یک نفر را زخمی کرد و یک نفر را زخمی کرد. سه نفر از مجروحان به شدت مجروح شدند.

An unhinged North Carolina state Senate candidate live-posted his own armed standoff with cops Monday, posting alarming updates from the woods as he claimed officers were closing in on him.

Jonathan D. Miller, the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina’s 16th Senate District in the suburbs of Raleigh, was taken into custody Monday afternoon with no shots fired, WRAL reported.

Miller began posting Sunday night that he intended to take his own life — then gave live updates when cops showed up to his apartment in Cary, outside Raleigh, Monday morning.

Miller refused an order to keep his hands away from a pistol at his hip and then ran into some nearby woods, he told WRAL.

“The whole police department is chasing me with guns drawn. This should be fun,” he wrote on X after fleeing.

Miller posted that he “has six shots and the high ground” as officers closed in, adding that he hoped police wouldn’t find him but that a confrontation would be “a hell of a show.”

“I f—-d up and talked to the negotiator on the phone long enough for them to box me in. They have dogs so I’m probably done for,” he later wrote.

Miller, who describes himself as a carpenter and former small-business owner, is running against a Democratic incumbent and a Republican contender in the Nov. 3 election.

He called a local news station during the standoff and explained his reasons for the suicidal threats.

“Last night I was pretty depressed and suicidal, and I sort of put a suicide note on X, and it has gone quite viral … I spent all night crying, and angry, and upset, and depressed, and all the emotions. And this morning I was tired, but I had things I needed to do. And I didn’t kill myself,” he told WRAL.

“So I got up and made coffee … and while I was having a cigarette, a police officer approached me, knew my name, saw that I had a holstered revolver on my hip, so he drew his weapon and told me to keep my hands away from mine. I told him I was going to refuse that order, and I backed away slowly until I was far enough away from him to turn and run, and then I turned and ran into the woods,” he continued.

If you are struggling with suicidal thoughts or are experiencing a mental health crisis and live in New York City, you can call 1-888-NYC-WELL for free and confidential crisis counseling. If you live outside the five boroughs, you can dial the 24/7 National Suicide Prevention hotline at 988 or go to SuicidePreventionLifeline.org.
news.content:
پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. یکی از نامزدهای مجلس سنای ایالت کارولینای شمالی در روز دوشنبه درگیری مسلحانه خود را با پلیس منتشر کرد و به‌روزرسانی‌های نگران‌کننده‌ای را از جنگل منتشر کرد زیرا ادعا می‌کرد که افسران به او نزدیک شده‌اند. جاناتان دی. میلر، نامزد آزادی‌خواه برای ناحیه کارولینای شمالی در بعدازظهر شانزدهم بعدازظهر به منطقه سناتوری در منطقه RSS منتقل شد. WRAL گزارش داد که شلیک شده است. میلر یکشنبه شب شروع به انتشار پستی کرد که قصد داشت جان خود را بگیرد - سپس وقتی صبح دوشنبه پلیس ها به آپارتمان او در کری، خارج از رالی آمدند، به روز رسانی زنده داد. میلر از دستوری برای دور نگه داشتن دستانش از تپانچه در ناحیه لگن خودداری کرد و سپس به چند جنگل مجاور برخورد کرد. میلر پست کرد که "شش گلوله و ارتفاع دارد" در حالی که افسران بسته شدند، و اضافه کرد که امیدوار است پلیس او را پیدا نکند اما درگیری "یک نمایش جهنمی" خواهد بود.
او بعداً نوشت: "من با مذاکره کننده صحبت کردم و آنقدر تلفنی صحبت کردم که آنها مرا داخل جعبه کنند. آنها سگ دارند، بنابراین احتمالاً من تمام شده ام." میلر، که خود را نجار و صاحب کسب و کار کوچک سابق معرفی می‌کند، در انتخابات 3 نوامبر با یکی از دموکرات‌ها و یک رقیب جمهوری‌خواه رقابت می‌کند. او در حین بن‌بست با یک ایستگاه خبری محلی تماس گرفت و دلایل خود را برای تهدیدهای خودکشی توضیح داد.

The latest “Saturday Night Live UK” soared with host Cynthia Erivo — and a wickedly funny "Wicked" parody. Meanwhile on "Weekend Update," co-anchors Paddy Young and Ania Magliano took several shots at Meghan Markle’s dad Thomas Markle Sr.’s child porn scandal. This was always going to be the mandatory part of the process, the walking-in-the-door part, where just being John Harbaugh was going to have to carry the day. The Giants have been an unserious operation for years; from the moment they affixed Harbaugh’s signature to the bottom of his contract, that changed in theory.

After that it was all on Harbaugh himself to make sure it changed in practice, too.

It has changed in practice. Already. Just seven weeks in, heading into the most satisfying bye week imaginable.

Get texts from Paul Schwartz with all the latest Giants news and insights, exclusive to Sports+ subscribers.

The Giants were – pick your adjective – dysfunctional, non-professional, slap-dash, slapstick; you can go on and on. Harbaugh brought a sparkling resume and a gaudy winning percentage and a shiny Super Bowl ring, and that made an impact in all the superficial ways that don’t guarantee a thing, a promising script in need of a director.
news.content: بیشتر پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. این همیشه بخش اجباری فرآیند بود، بخش راه رفتن در درب، جایی که فقط جان هاربو باید روز را تحمل کند. غول‌ها برای سال‌ها عملیات غیرجدی بوده‌اند. از لحظه ای که امضای هاربا را به انتهای قراردادش چسباندند، از نظر تئوری تغییر کرد. پس از آن همه چیز به عهده خود هاربا بود تا مطمئن شود که در عمل نیز تغییر خواهد کرد. در عمل تغییر کرده است. در حال حاضر. فقط هفت هفته بعد، به رضایت‌بخش‌ترین هفته خداحافظی قابل تصور می‌رسیم. متن‌هایی از پل شوارتز با آخرین اخبار و بینش‌های غول‌ها، منحصر به مشترکین Sports+ دریافت کنید. غول‌ها بودند - صفت خود را انتخاب کنید - ناکارآمد، غیرحرفه‌ای، با سیلی خط تیره، شلخته. می توانید ادامه دهید و ادامه دهید هاربا یک رزومه درخشان و یک درصد برنده زیبا و یک حلقه سوپر بول براق به ارمغان آورد، و این به تمام روش‌های سطحی که تضمینی برای چیزی نیست، یک فیلمنامه امیدوارکننده که نیاز به کارگردانی دارد، تأثیر گذاشت.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

We acutely feel the loss of certain performers because their faces, physicality, and mannerisms become a constant in our lives over decades of performing. But a performer doesn’t actually need to throw their entire body into our field of vision for that loss to hit hard; such was the case with Mel Blanc, who originated the voices of most of the Looney Tunes characters in the 1930s, ’40s, and ’50s, and continued to play them until his death in 1989. And now such is the case with Eric Bauza, the voiceover artist who currently performed many of those characters, among others, and passed away at the age of 46 over the weekend.

Bauza wasn’t the first performer to capably take over Looney Tunes vocalizing; voice actors including Jeff Bergman, Greg Burson, and Billy West have all done multiple Bugs Bunny projects, for example, and could often tackle multiple characters. But Bauza’s participation in the series of Looney Tunes cartoons produced for HBO Max — over 200 were produced in total — meant that he had some of the most sustained voiceover work in that world since Blanc’s days. He also performed in the accompanying film The Day the Earth Blew Up and this year’s Coyote vs. Acme, two of the very best attempts to bring the Looney Tunes to the big screen (and both of which were nearly scotched by parent company Warner Bros.).

Here’s a sign of Bauza’s enormous versatility: On the weekend of August 28 earlier this year, he had two movies debuting in theaters, for which he voiced more than 15 characters: the aforementioned Coyote as well as the decidedly more adult-oriented horror film Buddy, where he reproduced the sounds of ’90s kids TV voiceover performances. That gave him a better 2026 box office track record than plenty of bigger on-camera stars. And those weren’t his only 2026 projects; he also did multiple voices for the DreamWorks cartoon Forgotten Island.

Indeed, the breadth of Bauza’s work over the past decade-plus was stunning, going from “additional voices” credits on Sony projects like The Emoji Movie and a Smurfs sequel to a series of DC Comics characters for various animation projects (he was Aquaman in Teen Titans Go! To the Movies) to a whole bunch of Looney Tunes (starting with just Marvin the Martian; later, almost always Daffy and Porky; sometimes Bugs Bunny and Elmer Fudd; occasionally Foghorn Leghorn; somehow Tweety, too) to Luke Skywalker in various Lego Star Wars specials — no small feat, given that original Skywalker Mark Hamill is an accomplished voice actor himself.

This is just a fraction of his filmography. It feels especially important that he was able to help create new Looney Tunes adventures, not just because their parent company hasn’t always been the most supportive and caring of that label, but because they are all-time cartoon characters who cannot easily be reconfigured for a celebrity. Not that it would necessarily stop anyone from trying to get Chris Pratt to play Bugs Bunny — which makes it all the more important that someone as energetic, versatile, and engaging as Bauza could be there to make the implicit case for not pursuing a pointless big-name celeb. Colleagues and friends and even casual acquaintances have been quick to point out Bauza was a welcoming, friendly guy with plenty of other talents including stand-up comedy and cartooning (he got his start on an ill-fated Ren & Stimpy revival!). His worth wasn’t limited to his vocal ability. But with his voice alone, he brought so many characters to life, and made so many people happy, whether or not they knew his name.

Here are some of Bauza’s best works and where to stream them:

Made with the express purpose of recreating the bursts of short-subject energy that introduced Bugs, Daffy, and all the rest to audiences decades ago, Looney Tunes Cartoons is nominally a six-season show of 80 episodes, but it’s really a compendium of 240 contemporary shorts made in a classic Looney Tunes style. This allows for a virtuoso showing from Bauza, playing multiple characters multiple times across a variety of premises and combinations.

A feature film spun off from the Looney Tunes Cartoons series, this is the most focused of the characters’ other features because it’s really just about Daffy Duck and Porky Pig (and zero basketball players), giving Bauza a feature-length showcase for one of his strongest achievements: His riled up, pitch-perfect take on Daffy. (His Porky work is tops, too.)

Of course, Wile E. Coyote doesn’t talk, at least not in this iteration. (Mel Blanc did give him a smoothly “supah-genius” voice in one sub-series of 1950s cartoons.) But Bauza is still on hand to provide vocals for other Looney Tunes mainstays, including the Coyote’s nemesis, the Roadrunner (yes, he got to do the “meepmeep!”). Incredibly, this movie was nearly vaulted for a tax write-off by Warner Bros.; there was a sense of sweet revenge when it came out this summer through another distributor and promptly made more money at the box office than almost anything else Warner put out this year. It’s currently only available on VOD but should be on a streaming service within a few more months.

There are a number of Lego Star Wars specials that feature Bauza as Luke Skywalker, and they’re all pretty fun, doing whimsically time-warped riffs on the original trilogy, sequels, and prequels all at once. Bauza’s performance confirms his talent for voicework that sounds consistent with an established character but never settling for simply a poor man’s imitation.

Sadly, this Lego Movie spinoff series is currently only available to buy, not stream from a subscription service. But the show is a lot of fun, and probably worth owning if you have any Lego Movie superfans in your household. It’s one of Bauza’s best “various voices” gigs, because while he does indeed do various miscellaneous characters, he also gets to do recurring ones like Unikitty’s enemy Master Frown, as well as Crankybeard and Old Timey Mustache Man.

Jesse Hassenger (@rockmarooned) is a writer living in Brooklyn. He’s a regular contributor to The A.V. Club, Polygon, and The Week, among others. He podcasts at www.sportsalcohol.com, too.

news.originalContent:
See more of our coverage in your search results.

Hulk Hogan’s daughter, Brooke Hogan, took aim at someone who she claimed is responsible for the $5.9 million sale of the late wrestling legend’s Clearwater, Fla. home in a series of emotional Instagram Stories on Sunday.

Hulk, whose real name is Terry Bollea, died of a heart attack at age 71 in July 2025 at his home.

Brooke shared a photo of Hulk’s home with a “sold” sign.

“Enjoy your dirty money,” she wrote. “You took my dad.”

It’s unclear who exactly Brooke is referencing with her claim.

Brooke, 38, explained that her and Hulk’s second ex-wife, Jennifer McDaniel, were the “nurse crew” that took care of the WWE legend. McDaniel and Hogan were married from 2010-21.

“The sick feeling is indescribable,” Brooke wrote. “This house was where dad and Jen envisioned growing old together. Where we brought him back to … surgery after surgery. Pool days. The smell of gasoline in the his garage. His workouts downstairs.

“We cooked, we watched Jerry Springer, we played music , we cried. I walked in that garage every visit and hugged him right when he’d open the garage door. I’d sit next to him for hours in the chair he died in.

“His whole environment, his energy, his work, his relationships: First Jen – who no one but me treated with respect. Then I was gone… the truth teller… I’m sure to everyone’s delight. And now it’s all gone. Sold for profit. Just like him… used for f–king everyone else’s gain. Saddest ending I’ve ever seen. You know who the f–k you are.”

Brooke, who shared past photos of her and Hulk, explained that she was there for him for 15 years before “vultures swooped in conveniently,” adding that she tracked every medication he had to take.

Brooke, who asked to be removed for Hulk’s will in the summer of 2023, went on to praise Jennifer and shared photos of the pair caring for Hulk at home and at the hospital.

“This woman spent more time in the trenches than ANY of us did,” Brooke wrote of Jennifer. “He LOVED her dearly. And she loved him. She wanted to be there till his last breath despite the trauma she endured that I witnessed .. She asked for nothing .She could have fought for money. She left with a tiny fraction, a Tahoe, and a 2 bedroom house. And vanished. No smear campaign. Just grace.

“… Their breakup was devastating for me. I loved her, but I knew my dad was in the best care with her too.

“… An I’ve had to hear everyone say  I’m the jerk for stepping away from the toxic behavior an brainwashing, fake greedy people… ‘I should have been there. Everyone else’ was there till the end.

“NO. They were there AT the end. To collect.”

Hulk and Jennifer were married in December 2010 at his home in Clearwater, and he filed for divorce in October 2021.

In February 2022, he shared that they were divorced in a post on X.

Hulk married Sky Daily in September 2023.

Hulk and his first wife, Linda, were married for 26 years before their divorce was finalized in 2009. They share Brooke and son, Nick Hogan.

Hulk’s manner of death was ruled natural, according to the Pinellas County Forensic Science Center records obtained by Page Six.

The report also stated that Hogan had leukemia and atrial fibrillation, or an irregular heartbeat.

پوشش ما را در نتایج جستجوی خود مشاهده کنید. دختر هالک هوگان، بروک هوگان، فردی را که به ادعای او مسئول فروش 5.9 میلیون دلاری خانه اسطوره کشتی در کلیرواتر، فلوریدا است، در یک سری از استوری های احساسی اینستاگرام در روز یکشنبه مورد هدف قرار داد. هالک، که نام واقعی او تری بولیا است، در 2021 سالگی در سن 2221 سالگی درگذشت. home.Brooke عکسی از خانه هالک با علامت «فروخته شده» به اشتراک گذاشت. او نوشت: «از پول کثیف خود لذت ببرید. "تو پدرم را بردی."
مشخص نیست که بروک دقیقاً به چه کسی با ادعای خود اشاره می کند. بروک، 38 ساله، توضیح داد که او و همسر دوم سابق هالک، جنیفر مک دانیل، "خدمه پرستار" بودند که از افسانه WWE مراقبت می کردند. مک دانیل و هوگان از سال 2010 تا 2021 با هم ازدواج کردند. این خانه جایی بود که پدر و جن تصور می کردند با هم پیر شوند. جایی که ما او را به … جراحی پس از عمل جراحی بازگرداندیم. روزهای استخر. بوی بنزین در گاراژش می آید. تمریناتش در طبقه پایین. «ما آشپزی می‌کردیم، جری اسپرینگر را تماشا می‌کردیم، موسیقی پخش می‌کردیم، گریه می‌کردیم. هر بار که می‌رفتم در آن گاراژ قدم می‌زدم و درست وقتی در گاراژ را باز می‌کرد، او را در آغوش می‌گرفتم. ساعت‌ها روی صندلی که روی آن مرده بود، کنارش می‌نشستم. کل محیط او، انرژی‌اش، کارش، روابطش: اول جن – که هیچ‌کس جز من به او احترام نمی‌گذاشت. سپس من رفتم… راستگو… مطمئناً همه را خوشحال می‌کنم. و اکنون همه چیز از بین رفته است. برای سود فروخته می‌شود. دقیقاً مانند او… برای سود بردن دیگران استفاده می‌شود. غم‌انگیزترین پایانی که تا به حال دیده‌ام.

news.originalContent:
The Democratic candidate for the US Senate has been the subject of Islamophobic attacks from Trump.

Detroit, Michigan – Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed has dismissed United States President Donald Trump’s anti-Muslim attacks against him, saying that they are an attempt to move the attention away from the president’s own record.

At a news conference in Detroit on Monday, El-Sayed said Trump is trying to distract from issues that matter to Americans – including petrol prices and the war on Iran – by accusing the Democratic candidate of being a “jihadist”.

El-Sayed called the attacks “deflections and deceptions based on no evidence”.

“They have nothing to say about solving the problems in your life. They’re not talking about you,” the Democratic candidate said of Republicans.

“They’re not talking about your gas or your groceries … They’re not talking about clean air or clean water. They’re not talking about any of the things that the government is actually supposed to solve. Why? Because Donald Trump has created those problems.”

At a rally in Michigan on Sunday, Trump unleashed repeated baseless claims against El-Sayed, accusing the Democrat of wanting to impose “Sharia law” on the country.

“He would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate,” Trump said. “I want him to have a metal detector.”

El-Sayed laughed off the suggestion that he may personally be a physical threat to Congress. “He knows I got those Wolverine claws,” he said, a reference to the sports teams of his alma mater, the University of Michigan.

The progressive Democrat and former public health official is locked in a close race with former Republican Congressman Mike Rogers, a contest that could decide the Senate majority for the next two years.

Rogers has made unfounded allegations linking El-Sayed to the Muslim Brotherhood, Hamas and Hezbollah a central point of his campaign.

On Monday, El-Sayed said most Americans reject such attacks.

“There are always a few small people who want to make America small like that. You see them; they’re very loud, and they bark,” El-Sayed said.

“The vast majority of folks in this state believe in a big America. They’re open-minded. They’re big-hearted. And the story of America is those who believe in big America, overcoming the deception, the distraction, the sad attempts of the small-minded to make us small.”

He added that “Michiganders are a lot bigger than that”.

El-Sayed also addressed Trump’s statements mocking his name and misrepresenting it as “Mohamed”.

“My name and my faith are not the reason you can’t afford your gas – not the reason you can’t afford your groceries, not the reason you can’t pay your rent, your mortgage, not the reason you can’t see a doctor,” he said.

(Photo by Charlie Neibergall/Getty Images)

In a heated, closely watched Senate race that could tip the balance of power in Washington, the Republican candidate is trying to distance herself from President Donald Trump. Her Democratic opponent, however, is doing the opposite: praising the president on certain issues and finding common ground where he can. What does this ironic twist say about America’s two-party system?

During two separate interviews that aired Sunday on ABC’s “This Week,” former Republican Iowa Rep. Ashley Hinson and Iowa Democrat Josh Turek each made the case that they are willing to break from their party ranks. (RELATED: Massive Political Tornado Grows Over GOP Strongholds)

Hinson previously said that she would be Trump’s “strongest ally” in the Senate if she won. However, on Sunday, she added a caveat. She will ally with Trump if a policy aligns with what’s best for Iowans.

“I think the president would consider me a little bit of a thorn in his side because when we do talk, I’m always asking him for something for Iowa,” she said. “And last week when he called, or a couple weeks ago when he called to check in, I was like, sir, we need to make sure the soybean deal — soybean deal gets done, right? So, I think it’s really important every time I have a chance to have the president’s ear, I’m going to ask him for something that Iowa needs.”

“I will be someone’s ally when they’re with me on the issues that are important to Iowa,” Hinson went on. “And if they’re wrong, I’m going to pick a fight with them, no matter who that is.”

She offered praise for the Trump administration’s border, immigration, and anti-DEI policies, yet pushed back on Trump’s rose-tinted view of the economy, which the president has described as the envy of the world.

“Well, sure doesn’t feel like it right now,” Hinson said.

She also broke with Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance over the recent ad from Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign, which featured Democrat Amy Acton’s biological mother. Ramaswamy drew bipartisan criticism because Acton’s mother, Donna Arthur, married and stood by a man whom Acton accused of raping her as a child. (RELATED: Attack Ad Featuring Ohio Democrat’s ‘Abusive’ Mom Backfires On Vivek Ramaswamy)

“Yes, it’s terrible,” Hinson told ABC News. “I think about it as a mom, and you think about your kids surviving childhood sexual abuse and having to relive that trauma on TV again. I think it’s absolutely terrible, and I think they should take the ad down.”

Throughout his own interview, Turek made it a point to criticize Trump but also noted areas in which they can find common ground.

Describing himself as a “commonsense prairie populist,” Turek said he is advocating for “a livable wage, affordable housing, affordable health care, affordable pharmaceuticals, drinkable water, addressing Iowa’s cancer rate, functioning public schools, infrastructure, and addressing corruption.”

“I find that even ardent Republicans agree with me,” he said. “If there’s been any shift, it’s been socially.”

Turek also praised Trump’s crackdown on the Southern Border and said that the president has “accurately identified” the problems American voters are concerned about.

“He’s done a better job on the border than Biden, for sure,” he said. “I agree with him that we need to drive private equity out of housing. I would also like to see us drive private equity out of housing, healthcare, and nursing homes. And I agree with him that we should have no tax on tips, overtime, and Social Security.”

“I think that Trump accurately identified the problem,” Turek went on, appearing to reference Trump’s 2024 campaign. “That’s why I don’t vilify people for voting for Trump. He said, ‘You know, your grocery prices are too high. The system is corrupt. I’m going to lower your electric bill. I’m going to keep us out of forever wars.’ But the result has been more and more consolidation of wealth and power to a handful of individuals.”

Both Hinson and Turek’s attempts to highlight their independent streaks show the extent to which Americans are ideologically diverse and how they often do not fit into categories imposed on them by the two national parties.

On a range of issues, whether it is taxes, abortion, or foreign policy, Americans tend to hold views that conflict with the interests of the party, as well as the politician they vote for. For example, many Americans are sick of Middle East wars and foreign intervention, yet will vote for a Republican because they agree on lowering taxes. Other Americans are fine with the federal government enforcing antitrust law on big tech corporations, yet also believe that regulations on small businesses should be kept to a bare minimum. On foreign policy, some Americans support sending aid to Ukraine but not Israel. Others support both, while some support neither.

The political duopoly of Republicans and Democrats cannot answer these nuanced differences, which seem to be more prevalent in younger generations who are cynical about how the federal government functions. It is possible that in the near future, younger Americans will become sick of tribal politics and the complete failure of both parties to address the basics. Instead, they will look to independent candidates without strict ideological platforms or shameless loyalty to either party.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images)

Some Israelis are attacking Jewish billionaire Bill Ackman for describing how prominent Israeli candidates for the Knesset are perceived by Americans ahead of the country’s Tuesday election.

On Sunday morning, the Pershing Square hedge fund manager said that although he did not want to weigh in on the Israeli prime minister debate, he wanted to “share one point of view from the perspective of someone who has an understanding of how Israel is perceived in America.”

Ackman singled out Israel’s Minister of National Security, Itamar Ben-Gvir, and Minister of Finance, Bezalel Smotrich, saying they have caused the country “enormous reputational damage” as international media presents their statements and actions as representative of all Israelis.

He argued that a government without the two ministers would signal that Israel is moving on, allowing the country to rebuild its credibility, expand the Abraham Accords and strengthen its relationship with both major U.S. political parties.

I said I wasn’t going to weigh in on who should be prime minister of Israel as that is a decision for Israeli citizens. I did, however, want to share one point of view from the perspective of someone who has an understanding of how Israel is perceived in America. Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich have caused Israel enormous reputational damage with their statements and actions which are presented in the global media as representing the voice and will of all Israelis. As such, a government formed without Ben-Gvir and Smotrich will send a message to the rest of the world that Israel is turning a new page. This will allow Israel to rebuild lost credibility, increase the opportunity for an expansion of the Abraham Accords, and enjoy a better relationship with Democrats and Republicans and Americans at large.

Ben-Gvir and Smotrich’s controversial views have drawn international criticism, including from the United States, a major financial and diplomatic backer of Israel.

Smotrich has said it might have been “justified and moral” to let 2 million Palestinian civilians die of hunger to pressure the release of Israeli hostages taken by Hamas on Oct. 7. He also suggested that his call to “wipe out” the West Bank town of Huwara was merely a “slip of the tongue.”

Ben-Gvir has made similarly inflammatory comments, drawing condemnation from the U.S. State Department for saying that the Israelis’ right to use roads between Judea and Samaria is “more important than the right to movement for Arabs.”

Ben-Gvir faced further international backlash Sunday after bragging that his men had confiscated an “improvised cake” made by Palestinian “terrorist” prisoners using saved rations. He said the prisoners had prepared the cake to celebrate Tuesday if his party loses the election.

“The prisoners were brought to disciplinary trial and transferred to solitary confinement,” Ben-Gvir said before calling for party votes.

Despite the candidates’ controversial reputations abroad, prominent Israelis responded to Ackman’s post by defending Ben-Gvir and Smotrich as products of Israel’s political system and the fears of Israelis on the political right.

Channel 14 journalist and former Communications Adviser to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Gilad Zwick, began his lengthy defense by saying Israelis across the political spectrum have a “deep appreciation” for Ackman as he “[stands] up for Israel and [confronts] antisemitism.”

Although Zwick said he has not and will not vote for Ben-Gvir and Smotrich, he supports including them in the government, arguing that “much of the commentary about them abroad misses why so many Israelis support them.”

He pointed to Israel’s political system, suggesting that while Netanyahu often avoids being photographed with Ben-Gvir, he has relied on Ben-Gvir to help assemble a governing coalition.

Zwick added that voters on the political right continue to support Ben-Gvir and Smotrich because of their tough stances on Palestine. These voters see themselves as an island surrounded by a vast Arab and Muslim region, facing enemies who “have shown that they will spend years planning how to murder our children in the most horrific ways imaginable.”

“For many Israelis, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich’s tough stance sends an essential message: do not test us,” the former communications adviser said in defense of the candidates. “We will not rely on your goodwill. We will not gamble our children’s lives again on the belief that you have become more moderate, that you are deterred or that you have too much to lose.”

Ackman thinks that the job of the Israeli government is to look good in the eyes of the gentiles instead of defending its citizens against the Jihad. Sad! Pro tip Bill: people respect you when you are strong.

Another Knesset candidate, Yishai Fleisher, offered a more concise response, saying, “Ackman thinks that the job of the Israeli government is to look good in the eyes of the Gentiles instead of defending its citizens against the Jihad. Sad!”

National security and geopolitics researcher Khaled Hassan took a different approach, arguing that “it makes little difference who Israelis elect,” because the “overwhelming majority of Muslims in the Arab world and beyond are not going to abandon their hostility towards Israel and antisemitism simply because its government changes.”

Hassan said that when he was a Muslim antisemite, his hatred and hostility toward Israel had little to do with who held office. He added that Ben-Gvir and Smotrich are merely “convenient excuses” for people like him who would hate Israel regardless.

“Look at the political leadership in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and elsewhere in the Arab world. Look at their blatant antisemitism,” Hassan concluded. “Why does their conduct so rarely lead people to suggest that Muslims as a whole are antisemitic, while the actions and rhetoric of Ben-Gvir and Smotrich are routinely used to portray Israel as a nation of extremists?”

Polls compiled by the Jewish Telegraphic Agency suggest Ben-Gvir’s far-right Otzma Yehudit party could gain one or two seats, while Smotrich’s Religious Zionist Party is expected to lose one seat or maintain its current representation in Tuesday’s election. Both parties are expected to remain minorities, leaving their influence dependent on Netanyahu’s ability to maintain a right-wing governing coalition with a majority.

American businesses warned that higher energy costs could drive additional price increases as existing contracts expire, according to a Federal Reserve report released Oct. 14.

Companies in several regions expected to raise prices as they renegotiated agreements covering supplies and deliveries, the Fed’s October Beige Book reported. The findings suggest households could face additional costs as businesses adjust contracts that have temporarily limited their exposure to rising expenses.

Businesses expected that “prices will increase further in the coming months,” the report stated, citing uncertainty surrounding energy costs and tariffs. Higher diesel prices were already moving through supply chains through fuel surcharges, while other companies faced pressure from insurance and commodity costs.

Those increases were meeting resistance from customers. Consumer-facing businesses reported tighter profit margins and responded with selective price increases, promotions and menu changes designed to reduce expenses.(RELATED: Wholesale Inflation Spikes To Highest Level In 4 Years)

The pressure was apparent in the Kansas City Fed’s district, where businesses reported higher diesel and shipping costs alongside inventory delays. Most firms said they could pass those costs to consumers, although service businesses had less room to raise prices. Suppliers, distributors and customers were renegotiating terms to protect their margins.

Businesses in the Cleveland Fed’s district also reported rising costs tied to fuel and tariffs. Selling prices increased strongly as companies passed along expenses, while higher fuel prices continued to dampen consumer demand.

Consumers were already absorbing a sharp increase in energy expenses. Gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in September and accounted for more than half of the month’s overall increase in consumer prices, Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed. Annual inflation reached 3.7%, up from 3.4% in August.

Corporate filings illustrate how fuel costs can reach customers with a delay.

Performance Food Group, which distributes products to restaurants, convenience stores and other businesses, said in its fiscal 2026 annual report that its diesel surcharges generally follow fuel-price changes by one month. The company also uses financial contracts to manage some of its exposure to fuel prices.

Its fuel expenses increased $57.1 million in fiscal 2026, reflecting both higher prices and additional miles driven because of new business and acquisitions.

The distributor estimated that a hypothetical 10% increase in diesel prices would add approximately $43.9 million to annual operating expenses before partial offsets from customer surcharges and its fuel hedging arrangements.

(Photo by Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)

Sports betting companies prey on customers who lose the most money, but they place strict limits on those who consistently beat the house, CBS News reported Monday.

Sports gambling companies reward their biggest losers, gifting them VIP access to sporting events and signed memorabilia, according to CBS News. These same companies place severe limits on customers who win big, effectively cutting off those who consistently make winning bets on the platforms, CBS News said.

“You’re exploiting the losing bettor, you’re taking advantage of them, and guys like me get shown the door,” professional gambler Mike Manning told CBS News.

American sports bettors have wagered more than $700 billion since 2018, when the Supreme Court allowed for legalized sports betting in its ruling on Murphy v. National Collegiate Athletic Association, according to Legal Sports Report.

Of that revenue, 86% is contributed by 5% of users, according to advocacy group QuitGamble.

How the online sportsbooks treat their customers largely depends on whether those spenders are winning or losing. Neither FanDuel, DraftKings nor BetMGM responded to the Daily Caller News Foundation’s request for comment.

Manning bets using advanced analytical models; after registering for all the major sportsbooks, he started winning on every single one. Sportsbooks immediately limited the amount of money Manning could bet, CBS News reported. DraftKings limited Manning to $25 per wager. BetMGM restricted his limit to $5.

Professional gambler and responsible betting advocate Isaac Rose-Berman reported that he is unable to bet more than $15 on a prop bet through Fantatics.

Conversely, sportsbooks offer the biggest losers VIP status. (RELATED: Sports Gambling App Allegedly Uses AI To Target Those Most Likely To Lose Money On Bets)

“I put three or four hundred thousand into DraftKings in a span of a few months,” a recovering gambling addict Joe Early told ProPublica. While Early’s losses were mounting, DraftKings allowed him the opportunity to play basketball on TD Garden’s court with Celtics players. Early claims to have lost over $100,000 betting on DraftKings.

Former South Carolina attorney Chris Swett stole $2 million from his law firm to fund his gambling addiction, CBS News reported. Swett lost over $1 million on FanDuel in a two-year span, and as soon as he began losing tens of thousands of dollars a month, FanDuel connected Swett to a VIP host who began giving him tickets to NFL games when he bet big.

Sports betting has quickly become America’s most expensive pastime. Americans wagered $166 billion on sports in 2025, Yahoo Finance reported. That’s more revenue than the movie, book, music, concert and museum industries brought in combined. Furthermore, this figure doesn’t factor in the rapidly growing prediction market, which raked in $55 billion by July. Of this revenue, $19 billion was spent on contracts involving sports. These markets are under scrutiny for being unlicensed sports gambling, and ahead of the midterms, the markets are anticipating legal resistance to their status as non-sports gambling institutions.

news.originalContent:
The plaintiffs argue they are losing access to vital information media outlets covering Trump used to provide.

A group of private citizens has sued the administration of United States President Donald Trump over its restrictions on news outlets covering the White House.

“All of the Plaintiffs rely on the White House press corps for independent reporting about the president and his administration, and all of them use that reporting in a variety of ways in their scholarship, teaching, journalism, or advocacy,” says the lawsuit, filed on Monday in a federal court in New York.

The lawsuit is the first lodged not by the news outlets being banned, but by those who consume the news and rely on it for their work.

The plaintiffs include a human rights advocate, a media watchdog, a university history professor, a high school teacher, a legal journalist and a student journalist.

Each argues they need unbiased, diverse media reporting from the White House to do their work.

“I’m gravely concerned that the Trump administration’s restrictions on White House reporters are cutting off access to crucial information,” Peter Schmidt-Nowara, a high school social studies teacher in New York City, said in a statement.

“I joined this lawsuit because my students deserve to know what’s happening in their government and to hear from a free and independent press.”

Trump already faces several legal challenges to his practice of banning journalists from outlets he dislikes from accessing the White House.

Last month, he banned journalists from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico from attending news conferences at the White House. A federal judge later ruled the order was unconstitutional, a violation of the First Amendment, which protects freedom of the press, and ordered access be restored. However, the Trump administration continues to fight the ruling.

Last week, Trump dismissed reporting that he planned to evict journalists from the White House press briefing room and restore a swimming pool that was housed there starting in 1933. But he said he is still considering moving the press out of the briefing room.

“I am thinking about moving the Press, and putting them in a different location, but I will use that location for very badly needed space,” Trump said in a social media post.

Kenneth Roth, a senior fellow at Yale University and former executive director of Human Rights Watch, said the restrictions on press access were familiar postmarks in countries whose leaders have become authoritarian.

“Worldwide, I have seen how governmental leaders’ efforts to penalise independent journalists are a prelude to the rise of autocracy,” he said in a statement.

news.originalContent:
Investors react to Lula’s election victory with a sharp decline in the Brazilian real and concerns over increased spending and fiscal challenges.

Brazil’s real dropped against the United States dollar on the heels of Brazil’s President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva’s unexpected re-election after right-wing Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, led in the first round of voting earlier this month.

Brazil’s currency dropped against the dollar by 12 percent in spot trading. Bovespa stock index futures tumbled nearly 15 percent on Monday.

“I’m not surprised the real is sinking sharply; traders are covering their bets that assume a Bolsonaro victory and tighter fiscal policy,” Rachel Ziemba, adjunct senior fellow at the Center for a New American Security, told Al Jazeera.

Brazil’s stock exchange halted trading for 30 minutes. The Bovespa index fell 10 percent from its previous close, triggering a circuit-breaker safety mechanism and reversing a rally earlier this month amid expectations of a shift to the right after Bolsonaro won the first round.

Ziemba says Bolsonaro’s refusal to concede the election has driven some financial uncertainty.

“The market pressure is also amplified by the objections raised by Bolsonaro, but the scale of the victory suggests that the result will stand,” she said.

Interest rate futures had also reflected expectations that tighter fiscal policy under Bolsonaro would allow borrowing costs to decline.

“They [investors] assume more domestic spending and higher rates in Brazil. However, the real is still likely to be supported by strong commodity revenues,” Ziemba noted.

Stocks closed on Friday almost 7 percent above their level before the first round, while the Brazilian real was nearly 5 percent stronger against the US dollar.

Interest rate futures are up 3.1 percent, rising sharply after President Lula’s win. Interest rate futures had previously reflected a tighter fiscal policy amid expectations that Bolsonaro would oust the incumbent and that he would allow borrowing costs to decline.

Lula faces an increase in Brazil’s debt and will be challenged with protecting both social programmes and investment, with investors looking for signs of whether his gradual fiscal approach can bring borrowing costs down.

Lula’s team aims to produce a budget surplus of about 1.3 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) by 2030. That would leave money to cover part of the interest bill, reducing the need for fresh borrowing. But public debt already exceeds 82 percent of GDP, while pensions and other legally required spending limit where savings can come from.

“Lula’s policies have talked about spending cuts, but he has not gone into the details of how that is going to look,” said Divya Singaravelu, head of research at Meridian 1305 Capital.

Attention will now turn to Lula’s choice of finance minister and what it signals about his fiscal approach.

news.originalContent:
On November 3, Americans decide which party controls the US Congress for the second half of Donald Trump’s presidency.

On November 3, about 210 million registered voters will decide how much power Donald Trump has for the rest of his US presidency.

Trump is not on the ballot, but control of the United States Congress is. Made up of the House of Representatives and the Senate, Congress writes the country’s laws and controls federal spending.

In this visual explainer, Al Jazeera breaks down how the elections work, which races matter and what the results could mean for either party.

Held halfway through a US president’s four-year term, midterm elections decide the makeup of Congress.

All 435 seats in the House of Representatives and 35 of the Senate’s 100 seats are being contested, including special elections in the states of Florida and Ohio to fill the seats vacated by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Vice President JD Vance. Voters in 36 states will also elect governors.

House members represent one congressional district each and serve two-year terms, while senators serve six-year terms.

Midterm elections are also widely considered a referendum on the sitting president’s performance.

Since 1946, the president’s party has lost an average of 26.5 seats in the House and a handful in the Senate in midterm elections, according to Todd Belt, a professor of political management at George Washington University.

Beyond Congress and governors, voters will also elect state legislators and local officials.

Nadia Brown, a professor of government at Georgetown University, said that while national elections get most of the attention, “It is important to remember that local politics is where most Americans interact with government.”

She added that “It is the local propositions or referendums on ballots [that] will impact the everyday lives of people.”

Republicans hold majorities in both chambers. Losing either would give Democrats the power to block legislation and launch investigations into Trump’s administration.

Democrats need to gain three seats in the House and four in the Senate to take control. A 50-50 split in the Senate would leave Republicans in control, because Vance can cast tie-breaking votes.

Belt said a Democratic victory could significantly limit Trump’s ability to pursue his domestic agenda.

“If Democrats take one chamber, all non-government funding legislation will grind to a halt,” he told Al Jazeera.

The House of Representatives is the lower house of the US Congress.

Its 435 members each represent one local district and serve two-year terms, so every seat is contested every two years.

Seats are divided among the states by population, based on the US Census conducted every 10 years. California, the most populous state, has 52 seats, while the least populous, such as Wyoming and Vermont, have one each.

A party needs 218 seats for a majority.

Republicans currently control the House, with 218 seats to the Democrats’ 214, and one independent sits with the Republicans. Two seats are vacant, one last held by each party.

The new House will be sworn in on January 3, 2027.

Each district elects its own representative, and the party that wins 218 seats takes control, so a few narrow wins in close districts can decide the majority.

Belt estimates that about 35 House races could decide the majority. He predicts Democrats could gain about 15 seats, despite Republican redistricting that he says has given the party an advantage in nine additional districts.

“People generally vote straight ticket, meaning they will vote for all the candidates of one party, so this is likely to affect down-ballot races [as well],” he said.

A battleground district is a seat either party could realistically win. The graphic below highlights 12 of these key races to watch.

The Senate is the upper house of the US Congress.

Its 100 members, two from each state regardless of population, are elected statewide and serve six-year terms, with about a third of seats contested every two years.

This year, 33 seats are being contested in regular elections, alongside special elections in Florida and Ohio. Those two contests will fill the remaining two years of terms previously held by Marco Rubio and JD Vance.

Of the 35 seats being contested, Republicans hold 22, and Democrats hold 13.

Republicans currently have 53 senators. Democrats have 45, and two independents sit with them, giving the Democratic bloc 47 seats.

Democrats need a net gain of four seats to reach 51 and take control. Republicans can keep control with 50 because Vice President Vance can break tied votes.

The new Senate will be sworn in on January 3, 2027.

To win the Senate, Democrats must hold the 13 seats they are defending and flip Republican-held ones.

In Georgia, Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff faces Republican Mike Collins. Michigan’s open seat pits Democrat Abdul El-Sayed against Republican Mike Rogers, while Democrat Chris Pappas faces Republican John Sununu for an open seat in New Hampshire.

Republican-held seats offer Democrats opportunities elsewhere. In Maine, Senator Susan Collins faces Democrat Troy Jackson, who replaced primary winner Graham Platner after he withdrew in July. North Carolina’s open seat pits Democrat Roy Cooper against Republican Michael Whatley.

Ohio, Alaska and Iowa are also competitive, while Texas and Kansas have drawn growing attention as Democrats look for more routes to a majority.

Although Democrats face a more difficult path to a Senate majority than to control of the House, the growing number of competitive races has increased their chances of winning the chamber, according to election analysts.

The cost of living tops voters’ concerns, with rising petrol prices, housing costs and healthcare coverage squeezing household budgets.

Reproductive rights remain a major issue, while immigration and the state of US democracy are also on the ballot.

The US-Israel war on Iran and the rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI)` and data centres have raised further questions about security, jobs and energy costs.

About 210 million Americans are registered to vote, nearly eight in 10 US residents aged 18 or older, according to USAFacts, a nonpartisan organisation that compiles government data.

California has the most registered voters, with 23.2 million, followed by Texas (17.4 million) and Florida (13.6 million). Together, they account for about 26 percent of all registered voters.

Wyoming (278,468), Vermont (459,455) and Alaska (603,310) have the fewest.

A Pew Research Center survey conducted from September 28 to October 4 found that 44 percent of registered voters backed the Democratic candidate in their district, compared with 36 percent for the Republican. Five percent support another candidate, and 15 percent are unsure.

Men are evenly split, with 42 percent backing each party, while women favour Democrats by 45 percent to 31 percent.

The graphic below shows how voting preferences differ by gender, race, age, education and party affiliation.

Fewer Americans vote in midterms than in presidential elections. Since 1944, average turnout has been about 42 percent in midterms, compared with 58 percent in presidential races.

A Democratic House could block Republican legislation and use its committees to investigate the Trump administration. It would also hold the power to impeach the president, which only the House can do.

Control would also give Democrats leverage over government funding. Every bill needs approval from both chambers, so a Republican Senate could not pass laws on its own.

Belt expects a Democratic-controlled House to lead to more confrontations over federal spending, including the 12 annual bills needed to fund federal agencies. That raises the possibility of further government shutdowns, when funding lapses and many federal services stop.

Belt also believes that Trump could turn increasingly to foreign policy if his domestic agenda faces opposition in Congress.

“Traditionally, presidents facing divided government in their last two years pivot to foreign policy almost exclusively. I think the same will be true for Trump,” he said.

A Democratic Senate could block legislation and reject presidential nominees, including federal judges, Supreme Court justices, cabinet officials and ambassadors.

That makes Senate control consequential beyond the next two years. Federal judges serve for life, shaping rulings long after a presidency ends.

The Senate also holds the trial if the House impeaches a president. Removing a president from office requires a two-thirds majority, a threshold neither party is likely to reach.

No. Trump would remain president and could veto legislation, and overriding a veto requires a two-thirds vote in each chamber.

Senate rules also require 60 votes to end debate on most legislation, though some budget bills can pass with a simple majority. A narrow majority therefore does not guarantee a party can pass its programme.

A Democratic House could open impeachment proceedings against Trump, who has already been impeached twice. However, removing a president from office requires a two-thirds majority in the Senate.

Belt considers another impeachment unlikely.

“There will definitely be investigations,” he told Al Jazeera, but added, “There will not likely be another impeachment because Democrats tried that twice and Republicans rallied behind Trump.”

Results will begin emerging after the first polls close at 6pm Eastern time (23:00 GMT) on November 3, but some close races could take days to resolve.

Election night results are preliminary. Final tallies can take days or sometimes weeks as officials count mail-in, provisional and other outstanding ballots before certifying the results, and the pace varies by state.

“In some states, it may take up to a week or more,” Belt said.

Some contests may go further. In Georgia, if no Senate candidate wins a majority, the race goes to a run-off election on December 1.

Belt warned that early results could give a misleading picture of the outcome. Because Republicans have historically been less likely than Democrats to vote by mail, some states could initially appear to favour Republican candidates before later-counted ballots narrow or reverse their leads. This is known as the “red mirage”. In states that count mail ballots first, the reverse can happen.

A delay in counting or a change in which candidate is leading does not, by itself, indicate electoral fraud.

The vote will decide who writes legislation, scrutinises the administration and controls federal spending, setting the balance of power for the rest of Trump’s term.
news.content: در 3 نوامبر، آمریکایی‌ها تصمیم می‌گیرند که کدام حزب کنگره آمریکا را برای نیمه دوم ریاست‌جمهوری دونالد ترامپ کنترل کند. در 3 نوامبر، حدود 210 میلیون رای‌دهنده ثبت‌نام شده تصمیم می‌گیرند که چقدر قدرت دونالد ترامپ برای بقیه دوره ریاست‌جمهوری آمریکا دارد. ترامپ در صندوق رأی نیست، اما کنترل کنگره ایالات متحده است. کنگره که از مجلس نمایندگان و سنا تشکیل شده است، قوانین کشور را می نویسد و مخارج فدرال را کنترل می کند. در این توضیح تصویری، الجزیره نحوه عملکرد انتخابات، رقابت‌ها و نتایجی که می‌تواند برای هر یک از طرفین داشته باشد را شرح می‌دهد. انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای که در نیمه‌ی راه دوره چهار ساله رئیس‌جمهور ایالات متحده برگزار می‌شود، تشکیل کنگره را تعیین می‌کند. همه 435 کرسی مجلس نمایندگان و 35 کرسی از 100 کرسی سنا در حال رقابت هستند، از جمله انتخابات ویژه در ایالت های فلوریدا و اوهایو برای پر کردن کرسی های خالی شده توسط مارکو روبیو وزیر امور خارجه ایالات متحده و معاون رئیس جمهور JD Vance. رای دهندگان در 36 ایالت نیز فرمانداران را انتخاب خواهند کرد. اعضای مجلس نمایندگان هر یک از یک ناحیه کنگره هستند و دوره های دو ساله خدمت می کنند، در حالی که سناتورها دوره های شش ساله را خدمت می کنند. به گفته تاد بلت، استاد مدیریت سیاسی در دانشگاه جورج واشنگتن، انتخابات میان دوره ای نیز به طور گسترده به عنوان یک همه پرسی در مورد عملکرد رئیس جمهور فعلی در نظر گرفته می شود. از سال 1946، حزب رئیس جمهور به طور متوسط ​​26.5 کرسی در مجلس نمایندگان و تعداد انگشت شماری از کرسی های مجلس سنا را در انتخابات میان دوره ای از دست داده است.

news.originalContent:
(Photo by Jay L. Clendenin/Getty Images)

If you are trying to ship a package before Christmas this year, via ground or air, brace for some sticker shock.

Diesel fuel prices have surged over 60 percent since the end of February, while jet fuel recently hit a record high of $206 per barrel in October. In response to ongoing price spikes, global delivery giants United Parcel Service and FedEx are set to increase their fuel surcharges to record highs going into the holiday season, according to Reuters, which cited the TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index. (RELATED: Hidden Cost Of War That Trickles Down To Your Grocery Bill Set To Explode In 2027)

UPS’s fuel surcharge, based on the average price of diesel calculated by the U.S. Energy Information Administration, currently stands at 29.5 percent, Reuters reported. FedEx’s stands at 29 percent.

This is a major increase compared to the first quarter of 2021, when the average price of diesel was under $3 per gallon. At that time, the average fuel surcharge for a base shipping rate stood at 7.75 percent, according to the TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index.

Mingshu Bates, the chief analytics officer at AFS Logistics, said that even if diesel prices were to drop to those levels once again, the shipping surcharges would still remain over 20 percent due to changes in how delivery companies calculate fees and new pricing formulas, according to Reuters.

Since it began Feb. 28, the Iran War has imposed an estimated cost of nearly $2,000 on the average American household, according to Mark Zandi, the chief economist at financial intelligence firm Moody’s Analytics. Zandi factored in the cost of military operations, interest rate trends, and overall fuel costs. Higher energy expenses accounted for the vast majority of the total. (RELATED: Costco Raises Motor Oil Price, Caps Customer Purchases As Iran War Drags On)

According to a study from Brown University’s Climate Solutions Lab, total consumer spending on extra gasoline and diesel has surpassed $100 billion since the war began. Zandi’s analysis found that $1,100 of the total cost per household can be attributed to rising energy costs. Consumers are paying more at the pump for their own vehicles, but are also feeling a pinch from increased fuel costs for freight transit such as long-haul trucks and cargo planes.
news.content:
(عکس از Jay L. Clendenin/Getty Images)
اگر می‌خواهید بسته‌ای را قبل از کریسمس امسال، از طریق زمین یا هوا ارسال کنید، خود را برای ضربه‌های برچسبی آماده کنید. قیمت سوخت دیزل از پایان فوریه بیش از 60 درصد افزایش یافته است، در حالی که سوخت جت اخیراً در ماه اکتبر به رکورد 206 دلار در هر بشکه رسیده است. به گزارش رویترز که به نقل از شاخص حمل و نقل TD Cowen/AFS، در واکنش به جهش‌های مداوم قیمت‌ها، غول‌های تحویل جهانی United Parcel Service و FedEx قرار است هزینه‌های اضافی سوخت خود را به بالاترین میزان در فصل تعطیلات افزایش دهند. (مرتبط: هزینه پنهان جنگ که به صورت حساب خواربار شما می رسد که در سال 2027 منفجر می شود)
هزینه اضافی سوخت UPS، بر اساس میانگین قیمت گازوئیل محاسبه شده توسط ایالات متحده رویترز گزارش داد که اداره اطلاعات انرژی در حال حاضر 29.5 درصد است. فدرال اکسپرس 29 درصد است. این یک افزایش بزرگ در مقایسه با سه ماهه اول سال 2021 است، زمانی که میانگین قیمت دیزل زیر 3 دلار در هر گالن بود. در آن زمان، بر اساس شاخص TD Cowen/AFS Freight Index، میانگین هزینه اضافی سوخت برای نرخ پایه حمل و نقل 7.75 درصد بود. بر اساس گزارش رویترز، مینگشو بیتس، مدیر ارشد تجزیه و تحلیل AFS Logistics، گفت که حتی اگر قیمت گازوئیل بار دیگر به آن سطوح کاهش یابد، به دلیل تغییر در نحوه محاسبه هزینه‌ها و فرمول‌های قیمت‌گذاری جدید توسط شرکت‌های تحویل، هزینه‌های اضافی حمل و نقل همچنان بیش از 20 درصد باقی خواهد ماند.

اشاره ترامپ به جنگ با ایران است؛ موضوعی که نخست‌وزیر اسرائیل می‌کوشد آن را به یکی از محورهای کارزار انتخاباتی خود تبدیل کند.

اما این حمایت صریح، تضادی مهم را در روابط دو کشور برجسته کرده است: در حالی که آقای ترامپ بنیامین نتانیاهو را شریکی ضروری معرفی می‌کند، نظرسنجی‌ها نشان می‌دهند اکثریت آمریکایی‌ها به نخست‌وزیر اسرائیل اعتماد ندارند و نگاه به دولت این کشور نیز منفی‌تر شده است.

آیا این شکاف با تغییر نخست‌وزیر اسرائیل مکاهش می‌یابد، یا از تحولی عمیق‌تر در جامعه آمریکا خبر می‌دهد؟

بر اساس نظرسنجی ماه مارس مؤسسه پیو، ۵۹ درصد بزرگسالان آمریکایی گفته‌اند به نتانیاهو برای تصمیم‌گیری درست در امور جهانی اعتماد اندک دارند یا اصلاً اعتماد ندارند.

در نظرسنجی دیگری در ماه مه، ۶۲ درصد شرکت‌کنندگان دیدگاهی منفی به دولت اسرائیل داشتند.

در داخل حزب جمهوری‌خواه نیز شکاف نسلی قابل‌توجه است. فقط ۲۸ درصد جمهوری‌خواهان و مستقل‌های متمایل به این حزب در گروه سنی زیر ۳۵ سال، نگاه مثبتی به دولت اسرائیل دارند؛ این رقم در میان افراد پنجاه‌ساله و مسن‌تر ۶۸ درصد است.

این داده‌ها نشان نمی‌دهند که حمایت از اسرائیل در میان همه جمهوری‌خواهان از میان رفته، بلکه حاکی از تفاوت عمیق نگاه نسل‌های مختلف‌اند.

تل اشنایدر، خبرنگار سیاسی روزنامه تایمز آف اسرائیل، در گفت‌وگو با بی‌بی‌سی فارسی می‌گوید این تحول در اسرائیل «با نگرانی جدی» دنبال می‌شود.

به گفته او، «مردم بسیار نگران‌اند؛ چون دیگر مسئله فقط حزب دموکرات نیست که نتانیاهو روابطش را با آن به‌شدت تخریب کرده است. حالا این وضعیت به جمهوری‌خواهان هم کشیده شده است.»

آرون دیوید میلر، مذاکره‌کننده پیشین وزارت خارجه آمریکا و تحلیلگر موسسه کارنگی، در واشنگتن هم تأکید می‌کند که بخش عمده حزب جمهوری‌خواه همچنان حامی اسرائیل است و موضع انتقادی مطرح شده به وسیله‌ بعضی از شخصیت‌های جمهوری خواه لزوماً دیدگاه غالب حزب نیست.

به ارزیابی او، تغییر نگاه در میان دموکرات‌ها محسوس‌تر بوده و برخی از آنان خواهان مشروط کردن یا محدود ساختن کمک‌های نظامی آمریکا شده‌اند.

آقای میلر که از دوران جیمی کارتر تا جورج بوش پسر در دستگاه دیپلماسی آمریکا فعالیت کرده، می‌گوید: «هرگز روابط آمریکا و اسرائیل را، به‌ویژه از نظر سیاسی در داخل آمریکا، تا این اندازه تحت فشار ندیده‌ام.»

دیوید ماکوفسکی، پژوهشگر اتاق فکر راست‌گرای مؤسسه واشنگتن، دو عامل را از هم جدا می‌کند: سیاست‌های اسرائیل و تحولاتی در آمریکا که الزاماً به اسرائیل مربوط نیستند.

از نگاه او، گرایش‌های انزواطلبانه در سیاست آمریکا و دوقطبی‌شدن جامعه بر سر ترامپ، می‌توانند فارغ از هویت نخست‌وزیر اسرائیل بر افکار عمومی اثر بگذارند.

با این حال، آقای ماکوفسکی معتقد است تغییر سیاست‌های اسرائیل می‌تواند جلوی کاهش حمایت را بگیرد.

او می‌گوید: «شاید تغییر دولت فوراً همه‌چیز را دگرگون نکند، اما قطعاً می‌تواند جلوی ادامه ریزش حمایت را بگیرد و شرایط را بهتر کند.»

ماکوفسکی برای نمونه به برخورد خشونت‌آمیز علیه فلسطینی‌ها در کرانه باختری اشاره می‌کند و می‌گوید اگر مسئولان تازه عاملان این خشونت‌ها را بازداشت کنند و سیاست «عدم اغماض» در پیش بگیرند، چنین اقدامی می‌تواند به بهبود جایگاه اسرائیل کمک کند.

جنگ با ایران نیز می‌تواند به تشدید نگاه منفی آمریکایی‌ها به نتانیاهو دامن زده باشد.

آرون دیوید میلر، مذاکره‌کننده پیشین وزارت خارجه آمریکا، می‌گوید برخی جمهوری‌خواهان نتانیاهو را عامل ترغیب ترامپ به ورود به جنگ می‌دانند؛ جنگی که هزینه‌های اقتصادی و سیاسی سنگینی برای آمریکا داشته است.

با این حال، میلر تأکید می‌کند که مسئولیت اصلی تصمیم‌گیری درباره جنگ و پیامدهای آن متوجه خود ترامپ است؛ ضمن آنکه هنوز نمی‌توان مشخص کرد جنگ با ایران تا چه اندازه مستقیماً در کاهش اعتماد آمریکایی‌ها به نتانیاهو نقش داشته است.

تل اشنایدر با این ارزیابی فقط تا اندازه‌ای موافق است.

او می‌گوید: «صرفاً تغییر یک نام یا یک چهره، مشکلات را حل نمی‌کند. مسئله بسیار عمیق‌تر از این‌هاست.»

به اعتقاد او، پس از حملات هفتم اکتبر و جنگ‌های بعدی، حتی بخش‌هایی از چپ اسرائیل هم تمایلی به بازگشت به بحث راه‌حل دوکشوری ندارند. از این رو، جایگزین شدن نتانیاهو با سیاستمداری مانند گادی آیزنکوت الزاماً اختلاف نظر آمریکایی‌ها بر سر مسئله فلسطین را برطرف نمی‌کند.

خانم اشنایدر در عین حال معتقد است تغییر دولت می‌تواند روابط آسیب‌دیده اسرائیل با دموکرات‌ها، جمهوری‌خواهان و متحدان اروپایی را بهبود بخشد؛ روابطی که برای همکاری‌های امنیتی، از جمله مقابله با ایران، اهمیت دارد..

حمایت دوباره آقای ترامپ شاید برای بنیامین نتانیاهو سرمایه‌ای انتخاباتی باشد، اما جای پشتیبانی پایدار و فراگیر در جامعه آمریکا را نمی‌گیرد.

پرسش پیش روی اسرائیل تنها این نیست که چه کسی نخست‌وزیر می‌شود؛ بلکه این است که دولت آینده، به فرض تغییر نخست‌وزیر، با چه سیاست‌هایی می‌تواند شکافی را کاهش دهد که بخشی از آن به نتانیاهو مربوط است و بخشی دیگر از او فراتر می‌رود.

و در صورت ادامه حضور آقای نتانیاهو در صدر دولت اسرائیل، آیا این شکاف قابل ترمیم خواهد بود یا سرمایه حیاتی حمایت استراتژیک افکار عمومی آمریکا ازاین کشور کمرنگ‌تر خواهد شد؟

دونالد ترامپ در آستانه انتخابات پارلمانی اسرائیل، بار دیگر از بنیامین نتانیاهو حمایت کرده و از رأی‌دهندگان خواسته به او رأی دهند.

آقای ترامپ در شبکه اجتماعی تروث‌سوشیال نوشت پیروزی آقای نتانیاهو کمک می کند تا «کاری را که آغاز کرده‌ایم به پایان برسانیم».

اما این حمایت صریح، تضادی مهم را در روابط دو کشور برجسته کرده است: در حالی که آقای ترامپ بنیامین نتانیاهو را شریکی ضروری معرفی می‌کند، نظرسنجی‌ها نشان می‌دهند اکثریت آمریکایی‌ها به نخست‌وزیر اسرائیل اعتماد ندارند و نگاه به دولت این کشور نیز منفی‌تر شده است.

news.originalContent:
A political opponent has filed for a treason investigation into Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Avigdor Lieberman, chairman of the Yisrael Betenyu party, has appealed to Attorney-General Gali Baharv-Miara to begin a criminal probe into the Prime Minister. This probe would examine whether Netanyahu is intentionally trying to draw Israel into a confrontation with Iran just before the Oct. 27 elections, according to an announcement Lieberman posted to X on Monday.

“In the past month, Israel’s Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, has been pressuring the heads of the security establishment to take steps that could create a miscalculation vis-à-vis Iran,” stated Lieberman’s post, originally in Hebrew. (RELATED: JD Vance On Endorsing Netanyahu: I’ll Pass)

פניתי הבוקר ליועצת המשפטית לממשלה בדרישה לפתוח בחקירה פלילית נגד בנימין נתניהו באשמת בגידה. בחודש האחרון ראש ממשלת ישראל, בנימין נתניהו, לוחץ על ראשי מערכת הביטחון לנקוט צעדים שעלולים לייצר מיסקלקולציה מול איראן. הניסיון לגרור את מדינת ישראל ערב הבחירות למלחמה, יחד עם הנכונות להקריב את חיילי צה״ל רק בשל חשש מהפסד בבחירות, הם בגידה במדינה, בביטחונה ובחיילי צה״ל.

“The attempt to drag the State of Israel into war on the eve of elections, together with the willingness to sacrifice IDF [Israel Defense Forces] soldiers solely due to fear of losing the elections, constitutes treason against the state, its security, and the IDF soldiers,” the post continued.

The Ministry of Justice Spokesperson Division did not respond for immediate comment.

“The man has gone off the rails. One day he’s preparing a crypto bomb for us, and the next day an atomic bomb. He just said he had destroyed all of Iran’s bombs, and now he’s dropping bombs on Tel Aviv?” Lieberman told Israeli radio show 103FM on Monday, adding that the relationship between the military and political leadership has “never been as strained” as it is now.

הפרסומים על פערים בין הדרג המדיני לצה"ל בנושא איראן הם מופרכים ושקריים לחלוטין. מאז כניסתי לתפקיד שר הביטחון התיאום בין רה"מ וביני לבין צה"ל בנושא איראן הוא מלא - עם הישגים היסטוריים חסרי תקדים לטובת ביטחון מדינת ישראל. זהו השיקול היחיד - וכך יהיה גם בעתיד. אני קובע באופן חד משמעי שלא הייתה שום כוונה של ישראל ליזום התקפה על איראן לפני הבחירות בישראל - כאשר הבהרנו שבמידה ואיראן תתקוף את ישראל נגיב בעוצמה רבה, וכל הפרסומים בעניין שקריים לחלוטין. הניסיון של אנשי האופוזיציה לנצל את הפרסומים האלה כדי לתקוף את רה"מ ואותי ולהטיל דופי בשיקולינו - בשעה שאנחנו מנועים מסיבות מובנות מלהתייחס לפרטי הסוגיה האיראנית - הוא מביש וחסר אחריות. נתגבר גם על זה.

“This is the result of Netanyahu’s efforts to provoke a miscalculation with Iran. The chief of staff is strong enough to insist on upholding the law, and under the law, any action whose consequences could lead the State of Israel into war or a large-scale confrontation must be subject to a government discussion and decision,” he continued on 103FM.

Following these accusations, Defense Minister Israel Katz denied the strain between military and political leadership.

“The reports about gaps between the political echelon and the IDF on the Iran issue are entirely baseless and false…The attempt by opposition figures to exploit these reports to attack the Prime Minister and me and to cast doubt on our judgment —at a time when we are prevented for understandable reasons from addressing the details of the Iranian issue — is shameful and irresponsible,” he posted on X Monday, writing in Hebrew.

Lieberman’s Israel Betenyu is a right-wing party that was founded in the 1990s splitting from Netanyahu’s Likud. Upon its founding, its primary electorate was Russian-speaking secular Jewish immigrants to Israel.
news.content: یک مخالف سیاسی برای تحقیقات خیانت در مورد بنیامین نتانیاهو، نخست وزیر اسرائیل، تشکیل پرونده داده است. آویگدور لیبرمن، رئیس حزب اسرائیل بتنیو، از گالی بهارو میارا، دادستان کل درخواست کرده است تا تحقیقات جنایی علیه نخست وزیر آغاز کند. این تحقیق بررسی خواهد کرد که آیا نتانیاهو عمداً در تلاش است تا اسرائیل را به رویارویی با ایران درست قبل از اکتبر سال جاری بکشاند یا خیر. بر اساس اعلامیه ای که لیبرمن در روز دوشنبه به X ارسال کرد. در پست لیبرمن که در اصل به زبان عبری است، آمده است: «در ماه گذشته، نخست وزیر اسرائیل، بنیامین نتانیاهو، روسای نهادهای امنیتی را تحت فشار قرار داده است تا اقداماتی را انجام دهند که می تواند یک اشتباه محاسباتی در قبال ایران ایجاد کند. (مرتبط: جی دی ونس در حمایت از نتانیاهو: می گذرم) פניתי הבוקר ליועצת המשפטית לממשלה בדרישה פתוח בחקירה פלי בנימין נתניהו באשמת בגידה. בחודש האחרון ראש ממשלת ישראל، בנימין נתניהו، לוחץ על ראשרי מותעל לנקוט צעדים שעלולים לייצר מיסקלקולציה מול איראן. הניסיון לגרור את מדינת ישראל ערב הבחירות למלחמה، יחד עליכונת את חיילי צה״ל רק בשל חשש מהפסד בחירות، הם בגידה במדינה، טבוה ובחיילי צה״ל. در ادامه این پست آمده است: «تلاش برای کشاندن کشور اسرائیل به جنگ در آستانه انتخابات، همراه با تمایل به قربانی کردن سربازان ارتش اسرائیل تنها به دلیل ترس از شکست در انتخابات، خیانت به دولت، امنیت آن و سربازان ارتش اسرائیل است.» بخش سخنگوی وزارت دادگستری به من پاسخی نداد.

(Photo by AFP via Getty Images)

A hidden cost of war that will eventually trickle down to your grocery, gas, and heating bills is set to rise sharply in 2027 because of the contested Strait of Hormuz.

After 8 months of war, the critical chokepoint for global oil shipping has split into two routes: one side controlled by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard and the Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA), and the other corridor kept open by a U.S. naval blockade and forces escorting commercial ships on a route that hugs Oman’s coastline. Despite having a lane for ships that wish to bypass the PGSA, shipping costs are set to rise in 2027 if Iranian attacks on tankers continue apace or the war escalates before or after the U.S. midterm elections. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: The Iran War Is Going To Go Ballistic After Midterms)

(عکس از خبرگزاری فرانسه از طریق گتی ایماژ)
هزینه پنهان جنگ که در نهایت به قبوض خواربار، گاز و گرمایش شما خواهد رسید، قرار است در سال 2027 به دلیل تنگه مورد مناقشه هرمز به شدت افزایش یابد. پس از 8 ماه جنگ، نقطه انسداد حیاتی برای حمل و نقل جهانی نفت به دو مسیر تقسیم شده است: یک طرف تحت کنترل سپاه پاسداران انقلاب اسلامی و دیگری تحت کنترل سپاه پاسداران انقلاب اسلامی است. باز توسط ایالات متحده محاصره دریایی و نیروهای اسکورت کشتی های تجاری در مسیری که خط ساحلی عمان را در بر می گیرد. با وجود داشتن مسیری برای کشتی‌هایی که می‌خواهند PGSA را دور بزنند، در صورتی که حملات ایران به نفت‌کش‌ها به سرعت ادامه یابد یا جنگ قبل یا بعد از انتخابات میان‌دوره‌ای آمریکا تشدید شود، هزینه‌های حمل و نقل در سال 2027 افزایش خواهد یافت.
